# plot_electrostatic_isosurfaces { #mofography.visualize.plot_electrostatic_isosurfaces }

```python
visualize.plot_electrostatic_isosurfaces(
    potential_V,
    atoms,
    isovals=None,
    num_isosurfaces=10,
    cscale='viridis',
    step=1,
    base_opacity=0.3,
)
```

Create a single Plotly mesh trace for the electrostatic potential isosurfaces with correct scaling and hover info.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name         | Type   | Description                                                                           | Default    |
|--------------|--------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| potential_V  |        | 3D array of potential values in volts                                                 | _required_ |
| cell         |        | Cell matrix                                                                           | _required_ |
| atoms        |        | ASE Atoms object                                                                      | _required_ |
| step         |        | Step size for marching cubes algorithm. Higher values result in coarser surfaces.     | `1`        |
| base_opacity |        | Base opacity for the surfaces. Adjust this to make surfaces more or less transparent. | `0.3`      |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type   | Description                           |
|--------|--------|---------------------------------------|
|        |        | A single combined Plotly Mesh3d trace |
